risks.note: Ongoing conflicts and trade disruptions have the potential to impact supply chains, logistics costs and raw material availability.
Movements in the USD-INR exchange rate remain a significant cost driver for imported raw materials and components.

Changes in laminate prices, metals, energy costs and freight rates influence manufacturing economics; certain input costs have risen by roughly 3x, supplier lead times have extended from 4 to 7 weeks, and some suppliers have begun declining new orders.
Freight availability, shipping disruptions and container shortages continue to require active monitoring and mitigation.
The Company monitors evolving environmental compliance requirements and labour-law obligations applicable to its manufacturing operations.
The Board monitors customer and segment concentration as part of its ongoing risk review to ensure the revenue base remains adequately diversified.

Given the pace of change in PCB manufacturing technology (multilayer capability, surface-finish techniques, automation), the Company must continue to evaluate its equipment and process roadmap to avoid falling behind evolving customer specifications.

- The Company monitors evolving environmental compliance requirements and labour-law obligations applicable to its manufacturing operations.
- The Board monitors customer and segment concentration as part of its ongoing risk review to ensure the revenue base remains adequately diversified.
